title: Casper and the Asset
premise: Rafael Brightwater, a burned-out interpreter for a fragile peace delegation, is approached by Casper, a stranger who claims Rafael once saved their life—a favor Rafael has no memory of. Casper demands repayment in kind: help expose an attack engineered to look like an accident, timed to destroy the peace talks and bury the truth of what happened to Rafael during 'the incident.' As the two dig through layers of official lies, Rafael realizes the attack is tied to their own suppressed past and that someone inside the delegation wants them silenced. In the end, Rafael must choose between protecting the person they've come to love and revealing a truth that will end their career—and possibly their life—stopping the attack at the cost of everything but each other.
about_author: Ivo Vasquez is a former conference interpreter turned novelist who writes thrillers drawn from the corridors where diplomacy and deception meet. They live quietly in a coastal city, writing under a pen name to keep their sources—and themselves—invisible.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Insomniac and hollowed out by 'the incident,' Rafael works the margins of a doomed peace delegation until a stranger named Casper corners them with an impossible claim: Rafael saved their life, and the debt is now due. The beat is unease—the past knocking on a door Rafael bricked shut.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper lays out the demand: not money, but help proving that an 'accident' scheduled during the summit's final week is manufactured. Rafael refuses and walks away, then finds a photograph in their own coat pocket—one they never took. The beat is vertigo: reality loosening.

chapters.title: Interpreter's Silence
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Back in the delegation's rhythm of translated half-truths, Rafael notices a security briefing phrase that doesn't survive translation honestly—someone is editing meaning in real time. The emotional beat is professional dread: Rafael's sharpest tool detecting rot in the machine.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper traces the photo's origin to a shuttered logistics firm and a dead man whose identity was recycled into the delegation's security detail. Casper realizes the plot has institutional cover. Beat: cold clarity hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael confronts Casper; instead of answers, gets a bargain: forty-eight hours of cooperation, then Casper vanishes forever. Rafael agrees, telling themself it's only to disprove the whole thing. Beat: reluctant alliance sealed over bad coffee and mutual distrust.

chapters.title: What the Incident Was
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A flashback chapter: eighteen months ago, a convoy, an explosion ruled accidental, and Rafael as the sole witness whose testimony was rewritten before it was recorded. Present-day Rafael begins matching details. Beat: grief resurfacing as evidence.

chapters.title: The Delegation's Ghost
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper infiltrates a summit reception and identifies Deputy Chief Aldous Vane as the thread connecting the old convoy file to the new security plan. Vane recognizes Casper's face from somewhere he shouldn't. Beat: hunter briefly becoming prey.

chapters.title: Translated Lies
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. During a plenary session, Rafael deliberately mistranslates on purpose for the first time in their career—to buy time, to protect a source, to test Vane. Vane's reaction confirms guilt. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear of being caught.

chapters.title: Safe House Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Holed up in a safe house, Casper and Rafael map the attack: a gas main failure timed to the closing ceremony, blame assigned to the host nation's opposition. The math only works if one specific wing of the venue is empty. Beat: intimacy growing inside urgency.

chapters.title: The Memory Gap
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael finally asks why they can't remember saving Casper. Casper admits the debt story was a lever—but the underlying event was real, and Rafael's memory was chemically blurred during the official inquiry. Beat: betrayal and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Vane summons Rafael privately and offers promotion, protection, and a quiet transfer—if Rafael stops asking questions and hands over 'the stranger.' He mentions Rafael's sister by name. Beat: duty weaponized against loyalty.

chapters.title: Running the Corridors
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper lifts the operational schedule from a courier, discovering the attack moved up by three days. A tail follows Casper through the old town; a brutal escape leaves Casper wounded. Beat: the clock audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Stitches and Confessions
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael patches Casper's wound in a laundromat back room. Between sutures, truths surface: Casper's real name, Rafael's buried testimony, the first honest conversation either has had in years. Beat: love arriving without permission.

chapters.title: The Inside Man
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Following the recycled identity, Casper turns the dead man's former colleague, who confirms the 'accident' blueprint and names the trigger mechanism: a maintenance crew badge list. Beat: hope with a body count attached.

chapters.title: Badge List
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael uses interpreter access to photograph the credential roster, nearly caught by Vane's security chief. The list contains a name Rafael knows—the colleague who comforted them after the incident. Beat: paranoia turning inward; no one is clean.

chapters.title: The Colleague
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Rafael confronts the colleague, who breaks: they were coerced after the incident, their family threatened, and they've been feeding Vane updates on Rafael for months—including tonight. Beat: heartbreak; the last safe relationship burns down.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. With the timeline moved up, evacuation warnings would be ignored as sabotage. Casper proposes the unthinkable: let a smaller, controlled version of the 'accident' happen early, emptying the wing and exposing the mechanism publicly. Beat: moral cliff edge.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael must decide whether to trust Casper's plan or go to the delegation—knowing Vane controls both channels. A late-night argument becomes a declaration neither can take back. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: Dual POV, intercut. Execution night: Casper triggers the early diversion while Rafael manipulates interpretation live on the ceremony floor to move dignitaries out of the kill zone. Vane realizes mid-sentence what Rafael is doing. Beat: white-knuckle tension.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The blast comes—smaller, contained, undeniable. Investigators find the tampered infrastructure exactly where Casper ensured they'd look. Vane attempts to flee through the service tunnels; Casper intercepts him. Beat: catharsis with blood on it.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael gives the full statement they were denied eighteen months ago—naming Vane, the inquiry's fixers, and their own coerced silence. Career, clearance, and cover all burn. Beat: costly truth spoken aloud, voice steady.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, epilogue. Months later, Rafael interprets at a small, unglamorous arbitration hearing—honest work, modest stakes. Casper appears at the door with coffee and no debts outstanding. Rafael sleeps that night, and the next. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
